2.title: 07/14/2026: Chairman Bost, VSOs Host Press Conference On Take Care of America's Veterans Act
2.description: This sweeping veterans’ package includes the Maj. Richard Star Act, the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act, the Veterans’ ACCESS Act, and over 60+ bills to advance the largest expansion of healthcare, benefits, and services in decades for nearly 32 million veterans, their families, Gold Star families, caregivers, and today and tomorrow’s active-duty servicemembers.

338.title: 2020-01-29 Full Committee Hearing: Caring for Veterans in Crisis
338.description:
EventID=110417
On Wednesday, January 29, 2020, the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs will hold an oversight hearing entitled, “Caring for Veterans in Crisis: Ensuring a Comprehensive Health System Approach.”  The hearing will explore Veterans Health Administration (VHA) policies related to screening for suicide risk, care coordination for veterans at risk of suicide, the mental health environment of care on Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) campuses, and the extent to which VHA is maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment for veterans experiencing mental health crises.

343.title: 2019-11-20 Subcommittee on TM Hearing: The Status of EHRM Readiness
343.description:
EventID=110219

130.title: PTSD Awareness Month Message
130.description:
June is #PTSDAwarenessMonth. This month and every month, Ranking Member Roe encourages any fellow veteran who may be struggling to reach out and ask for help.

It's okay to not be okay.

PTSD is treatable and treatment works.

You are not alone in this fight.

4.title: “BAD PAPER & BUREAUCRACY: HOW CHARACTER OF DISCHARGE AFFECTS VULNERABLE VETERANS”
4.description: WASHINGTON – On Wednesday, July 15th, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., the Ranking Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, Congressman Mark Takano, will hold a roundtable focused on servicemembers' return to civilian life and how VA’s characterization of their discharge status affects their access to healthcare and benefits. Too often, veterans receive "bad paper" discharges, discharges that range between Honorable and Dishonorable, because of circumstances related to factors like race, sexual orientation, or actions caused by PTSD, TBI, or MST. Progress has been slow in addressing inconsistencies and inequities in the discharge characterization, upgrade, and review processes. And VA has long strayed far from Congressional intent in barring access to care and benefits. The roundtable will explore how DOD and VA must improve their policies and procedures to better fulfill their obligations to provide care and support to veterans.

10.title: “Continuing the Mission: Veteran Leadership in Civic Engagement"
10.description:
On Wednesday, June 24, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. ET to 12:00 p.m. ET, in room 360 of the Cannon House Office Building, the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Democrats will hold a roundtable discussion titled, “Continuing the Mission: Veteran Leadership in Civic Engagement.” 
 
This roundtable will focus on efforts to engage veterans in nonpartisan civic activities to increase education, awareness, and stability around governmental and election-related activities. Potential issues for Members and participants to explore include election protection and education, nonpartisan poll workers, confidence in the electoral process, and the role of veterans in strengthening faith in elections.

16.title: RM Takano hosted a Press Conference on the Major Richard Star Act Discharge Petition
16.description: The House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39) held a bipartisan press conference with his Major Richard Star Act discharge petition cosponsor, Congressman Raul Ruiz (CA-25). This legislation will end the “wounded warrior tax,” or the offset that keeps medically retired veterans from receiving their full Department of Defense retirement pay and their full Department of Veterans Affairs disability pay. The House is currently collecting signatures on the discharge petition to force a vote on the House floor.

20.title: Republicans vote down blast overpressure presumptive
20.description: Committee Republicans voted against a presumption of service connection for blast overpressure. Blast exposures are not a matter of happenstance during a servicemember’s enlistment; they are an occupational requirement critical to the operational readiness of our military. Blast overpressure is one of the most common yet overlooked injuries facing our veterans. Why are Republicans opposed to making it easier for veterans suffering from blast exposures to get care and benefits?

26.title: “Fighting for Solutions that Work to Prevent & End Veteran Homelessness”
26.description: The House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Democrats held a roundtable discussion titled, “Fighting for Solutions that Work to Prevent & End Veteran Homelessness”. The roundtable focused on the following topics: the state of veteran homelessness and the factors influencing data trends in veteran housing insecurity; the effects of policies and actions that undermine programs and models that have effectively reduced and prevented veteran homelessness in communities across the country; proposals to modify and enhance tools and strategies to end veteran homelessness.

40.title: “Protecting the Freedom to Build a Family: Fertility Care and IVF Access for Veterans.”
40.description:
On Tuesday, March 17, 2026, at 10 a.m., the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Democrats hosted a roundtable discussion titled “Protecting the Freedom to Build a Family: Fertility Care and IVF Access for Veterans.” 

Although VA has taken some steps to expand access to assisted reproductive technologies, including in vitro fertilization (IVF), in recent years, veterans still report difficulties in meeting eligibility requirements and readily accessing IVF treatments through VA. This roundtable will focus on: veterans’ current ability to access IVF at VA; whether VA is effectively educating veterans, VA providers, and community providers about eligibility for and processes to access IVF care; relevant IVF policy trends; and current and future legislation to address IVF access for veterans.   
 
WHO: 
Ranking Member Representative Mark Takano (CA-39), Democratic Member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee 
Jennifer Ross, Manager, Federal Policy, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America   
Rita Graham, Director of Government Relations, Service Women’s Action Network  
Sharon Arana, Policy Team Member, Minority Veterans of America  
Maureen Elias, Deputy Director, Government Affairs, Wounded Warrior Project   
Julie Howell, Associate Legislative Director, Paralyzed Veterans of America  
Naomi Mathis, Deputy National Legislative Director, Disabled American Veterans  
Kayla Williams, Senior Advisor, Vet Voice Foundation  
Alex Dobhailen, Veteran Advocate  
Dr. Ginny Ryan, Reproductive Endocrinology and Infertility Division Chief, University of Washington School of Medicine  
Dr. Alicia Christy, Former Deputy Director of Reproductive Health, Veterans Health Administration 
Georgette Kerr, Federal Government Affairs Consultant, American Society for Reproductive Medicine  
Karla Torres, Senior Human Rights Counsel, Center for Reproductive Rights  
Alyssa Hundrup, Director, Health Care Team, U.S. Government Accountability Office

41.description: VA has lost over 1500 physicians in the last year! Sec. Collins claims he can't hire or retain doctors because he can't pay them enough. But over a year ago, Congress gave VA the authority to pay doctors more under the Dole Act. The Secretary either doesn't know the law or is refusing to use it.

49.title: Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity Markup
49.description:
On Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at 2:30 PM, the House Committees on Veterans’ Affairs will hold a markup on the following bills: 

H.R. 982, Warriors to Workforce Act 
H.R. 5634, Veterans Flight Training Responsibility Act of 2025 
H.R.7049, Improving Mental Health Care and Coordination for Homeless Veterans Act 
H.R.7083, CRUISE Act 
H.R.7103, Improving Emerging Tech Opportunities for Veterans Act 
H.R.7141, Affordable Housing Guarantee Act 
H.R. 1803, Fair Access to Co-ops for Veterans Act of 2025 
H.R. 1957, End Veteran Homelessness Act of 2025 
H.R. 1965, Veteran Education Assistance Adjustment Act 
H.R. 3159, Improving SCRA Benefit Utilization Act 
H.R.5436, To amend title 38, United States Code, to prohibit an educational institution from withholding a transcript from an individual who pursued a course or program of education at such institution using Post-9/11 educational assistance 
H.R.7150, To amend title 38, United States Code, to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit to Congress a quarterly report on housing loans insured, guaranteed, or under laws administered by the Secretary, and for other purposes. 

Documents for the hearing can be found on the Committee Repository here: https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByEvent.aspx?EventID=118994

59.title: Will Congress step up for veterans? #veterans  #veteransbenefits #congress
59.description: Of course, veterans are willing to pick up the tab for one another. It's the military way: service before self. Veterans will always step up, but it's time for Congress to step up. We should never ask veterans to pay for the benefits of other veterans and their survivors.

66.description:

But VA just rescinded its support for the Love Lives On Act because "the admin changed." House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Democrats have not forgotten the mission- delivering benefits for deserving spouses and their families.
Rep. Morrisson

78.title: “Frontline of Fraud: Preventing Scams Against Servicemembers, Veterans, and Their Families.”
78.description: On Wednesday, January 21, 2026, from 10:00am ET to 12:00pm ET, in room 360 of the Cannon House Office Building, the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs – Democrats hosted a roundtable discussion titled, "Frontline of Fraud: Preventing Scams Against Servicemembers, Veterans, and Their Families." During this roundtable they discussed fraud schemes that targeted veterans and their families, such as predatory lending, fraudulent benefit schemes like those carried out by illegal claims mills, pension poaching, and claims sharks, and other practices identified by the U.S. Department of Veterans' Affairs (VA), Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), like romance scams and multi-level marketing tactics.

87.title: Securing the Path Forward: Safeguarding Veterans' Information in the Digital Age
87.description: This roundtable discussed recent staffing and policy changes at the Departmentof Veterans Affairs (VA) that has created a more complicated security environment for protecting veterans’ data. Further, Members and participants had the opportunity to discuss the legacy of DOGE, the growth, and use ofveterans’ data to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, and VA's ability to enforce security protocols across VAs' enterprise and its partners.

95.title: Protecting the Promise: The Past, Present and Future of Veterans' Benefits
95.description: On Wednesday, November 5, 2025, from 10:00 a.m. ET to 11:30a.m. ET, in 360 Cannon House Office Building, the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs – Democrats, held a roundtable discussion titled, “Protecting the Promise: The Past, Present and Future of Veterans' Benefits.” As the 119th heads towards the end of the year with growing chaos and uncertainty, it is necessary to look at how far we’ve come regarding veterans’ benefits; it’s also necessary to address the threats to that progress that we are currently facing. The roundtable focused on veteran benefit priorities, and they had a frank discussion about what’s happening under the leadership of the current administration.

99.title: Roundtable: Profit Over Quality: Examining the Effects of Private Equity on Veteran Healthcare
99.description: On September 9, at 10:00 a.m. ET, the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs Democrats held a roundtable to examine how profit-seeking behavior, including private equity (PE) acquisitions in healthcare, impacts veterans who receive care in the Community Care Network (CCN). This roundtable was an opportunity to explore the extent to which profit incentives in healthcare affect quality, access, and cost. As Congress considers the expansion of the CCN, we seek to ensure that the CCN better enables veterans to access healthcare without sacrificing care, quality, and access, and increasing costs to VA and the taxpayer, or funneling taxpayer money into bad actors' pockets.

100.title: HVAC & SVAC Press Conference on VA’s Decision to Ban Abortion Care and Counseling
100.description: September 3, 2025, at 2:00 PM, the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39) and the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Ranking Member Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) held a press conference in coordination with the Democratic Women’s Caucus and the Reproductive Freedom Caucus. The press conference focused on the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) proposed regulation to reinstate a near-total ban on abortions and bar VA providers from offering comprehensive pregnancy counseling, including information about abortion services.

109.title: "Beyond the PACT Act, Part two: Confronting Cumulative and Unseen Exposure Injury"
109.description: On Wednesday July 9, 2025 at 10:00 AM the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Democrats held a Roundtable titled, "Beyond the PACT Act, Part 2: Confronting Cumulative and Unseen Exposure Injury." Participants reviewed the occupational exposures affecting servicemembers in their daily lives that stretch beyond the battlespace. The roundtable was an opportunity for organizations, especially those that have historically been underrepresented in this conversation, to share their insights and concerns directly with policymakers. Participants discussed the legacy of Agent Orange exposures in locations not included in the PACT Act, sub-concussive impacts, traumatic brain injury, anomalous health incidents, infertility, heavy metal exposure, occupational health and safety, as well as others.

110.title: “Housing More Veterans Using the VA Loan Guaranty Program.”
110.description:
On Thursday, June 26, 2025, the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs - Democrats held a roundtable discussion titled “Housing More Veterans Using the VA Loan Guaranty Program.”    

The roundtable discussed the health of the VA loan program and mitigation measures to prevent veteran foreclosures, highlighting the importance of increased awareness of the program. It also explored various ideas on how VA could make the loan program easier to understand and use, thereby allowing more veterans to pursue the dream of homeownership.

114.title: Subcommittee on Health Legislative Hearing
114.description:
On Thursday, June 12, 2025, at 2:15 PM the Subcommittee on Health will conduct a legislative hearing on the following bills:
H.R. 785, The Representing Our Seniors at VA Act of 2025
H.R. 2068, The Veterans Patient Advocacy Act
H.R. 2605, The Service Dogs Assisting Veterans (SAVES) Act
H.R. 3400, The Territorial Response and Access to Veterans’ Essential Lifecare (TRAVEL) Act of 2025
Discussion Draft: To amend title 38, United States Code, to prohibit smoking on the premises of any facility of the Veterans Health Administration, and for other purposes
H.R. 3643, The VA Data Transparency and Trust Act, Discussion Draft: To direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to conduct a study to determine whether RNA sequencing can be used to effectively diagnose PTSD in veterans
Discussion Draft: The Health Professionals Scholarship Program Improvement Act of 2025
H.R. 3726, The Fisher House Availability Act of 2025
H.R. 1404, The CHAMPVA Children’s Care Protection Act of 2025
H.R. 2148, The Veteran Caregiver Reeducation, Reemployment, and Retirement Act
Discussion Draft: The VA Mental Health Outreach and Engagement Act

Documents for the Hearing can be found on the Committee Repository: 
https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByEvent.aspx?EventID=118378

115.title: Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations Legislative Hearing
115.description:
On Wednesday, June 11, 2025, at 2:15 PM the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigation will conduct a legislative hearing on the following bills:
H.R. 984, To amend title 38, United States Code, to direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide timelyequitable relief to an individual who suffers a loss based on an administrative error by the Secretary, and for other purposes
H.R. 1663, Veterans Scam and Fraud Evasion (VSAFE) Act of 2025
H.R. 3185, Personnel Integrity in Veterans Affairs Act of 2025
H.R. 3455, Veterans Affairs Distributed Ledger Innovation Act of 2025
H.R. 3482, Veterans Community Care Scheduling Improvement Act
H.R. 3483, Forcing Real Accountability for Unlawful Distributions (FRAUD) Act of 2025
H.R. 3494, VA Hospital Inventory Management System Authorization Act
Discussion Draft, To authorize the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out a program to modernize the electronic health record system of the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes
Discussion Draft, To amend title 38, United States Code, to prohibit the collection of a health care copayment by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs from a veteran after a two-year period if the delay in collection is attributable to a failure of an employee, official, or information system of the Department of Veterans Affairs to process certain information within applicable timeliness standards established by the Secretary

Documents for the hearing can be found on the Committee Repository: 
https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByEvent.aspx?EventID=118374

118.title: VA's Decided to End a Program Helping Veterans Stay in Their Homes - Press Conference
118.description: May 20, 2025, at 10:30 AM, the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39) held a press conference on VA’s thoughtless decision to abruptly end the Veterans Affairs Servicing Purchase Program (VASP)—a VA program that helped veterans experiencing severe financial hardship avoid foreclosure and stay in their homes.

The Trump/Musk Admin clearly doesn't care about how its reckless purge affects veterans. But HVAC Democrats DO CARE, and we WILL continue holding them accountable.

Soon after the Business Meeting concludes the Full Committee will begin the Oversight Hearing on “Accountable or Absent?: Examining VA Leadership Under the Biden-Harris Administration".

Documents for the hearing can be found on the Committee Repository here: https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByEvent.aspx?EventID=117557

173.title: The Subcommittee on Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs Markup
173.description:
On Tuesday, July 23, 2024, at 1:00 p.m., the Subcommittee on Disability and Memorial Affairs will hold a markup on the following legislation:

"H.R. 2971, Veterans Claims Education Act of 2023; H.R. 6362, Protecting Benefits for Disabled Veterans Act of 2023; H.R. 8792, Flowers for Fallen Heroes Act of 2024; H.R. 8874, Modernizing All Veterans and Survivors Claims Processing Act; H.R. 8879, Improving VA Training for Military Sexual Trauma Claims Act; H.R. 8880, Simplifying Forms for Veterans Claims Act; H.R. 8881, Rural Veterans’ Improved Access to Benefits Act of 2024; H.R. 8893, Preserving Veterans’ Legacy Act; H.R. 8910, Dayton National Cemetery Expansion Act of 2024; H.R. 9053, Veterans 2nd Amendment Restoration Act; H.R. 9054, Safeguarding Veterans 2nd Amendment Rights Act; H.R. 9057, Gulf War Survivor Benefits Update Act of 2024; H.R. 9055, Veterans’ Burial Improvement Act of 2024; and H.R. 9056, VA Insurance Improvement Act."

Documents for the hearing can be found on the Committee Repository here: https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByWeek.aspx?WeekOf=07212024_07272024

201.title: Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity Legislative Hearing
201.description:
On Wednesday, March 20, 2024, at 10:30 a.m., the Subcommittee on Economic Opportunity will hold a legislative hearing on the following bills:

"H.R. 6656, Stuck on Hold Act; H.R. 7323, To amend title 38, United States Code, to direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disapprove courses of education offered by a public institution of higher learning that does not charge the in-State tuition rate to a veteran using certain educational assistance under title 10 of such Code; H.R. XXXX, To amend title 38, United States Code, to provide for a limitation on the amount of entitlement to educational assistance payable for flight training under the Post-9/11 Educational Assistance Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs; H.R. XXXX, To amend title 38, United States Code, to provide for the restoration of entitlement of individuals entitled to educational assistance under the laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs who use such entitlement to pursue a course or program of education at an educational institution found to have violated certain prohibitions on advertising, sales, and enrollment practices, and for other purposes; H.R. XXXX, To amend titles 10 and 38, United States Code, to make improvements to certain programs for a member nearing separation, or for a veteran who recently separated, from the Armed Forces, and for other purposes; H.R. 6225, Expanding Home Loans for Guard and Reservists Act; H.R. XXXX, To amend title 38, United States Code, to authorize the use of Department of Veterans Affairs work-study allowance to carry out casework, policy making, and oversight related to the activities of the Department at certain congressional offices; H.R. XXXX, To amend title 38, United States Code, to update certain terminology regarding veteran employment; and H.R. XXXX, Fair Access to Co-ops for Veterans Act of 2024.”

Documents for the hearing can be found on the Committee Repository here: https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Committees.aspx?Code=VR00

219.title: Examining VA Appeals Process: Ensuring High Quality Decision-Making for Veterans’ Claims on Appeal
219.description: On November 29, 2023, at 11:00 a.m. (EST) the Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Subcommittee on DAMA will hold an Oversight hearing in 360 Cannon House Office Building, to discuss the quality of actions by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Board of Veterans’ Appeals (Board), including Board determinations on whether a Notice of Disagreement has initiated an appeal, Board remands of cases to the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) for further action or development, and Board decisions on veterans’ claims for VA benefits. The hearing will also examine the extent to which the VBA uses data from Board remands to inform its quality assurance and training programs, as well as the extent to which the Board uses data from orders by the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims to inform its quality assurance and training programs.

Harvey, Jr. and Adam Lambert Improving Servicemember Transition to Reduce Veteran Suicide Act and the Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute to it; H.R. 3738, To amend title 38, United States Code, to establish in the Department of Veterans Affairs the Veterans Economic Opportunity and Transition Administration, and for other purposes; H.R. 3816, Veterans' Entry to Apprenticeship Act; H.R. 5190, Military Family Protection from Debt Act; H.R. XXXX, Expanding Access for Onliine Veteran Students Act; H.R. 315.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities for Student Veterans
315.description: Before wrapping up last Congress, the Committee passed significant student veteran protections into law that will improve the quality of education offered to students nationwide, expand benefits for student veterans and their families, and give the State Approving Agencies responsible for approving courses the ability to crack down on poor performing schools. This Congress, our Committee will go further by guaranteeing a successful implementation of these protections, monitoring the quality of education for students temporarily using remote learning due to COVID-19, and ensuring unscrupulous institutions no longer can defraud student veterans of their hard earned benefits.

316.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities - Reducing Veteran Suicide
316.description: In the 116th Congress, the Committee worked tirelessly to develop and advance two bipartisan, bicameral packages to prevent veteran suicide. These bills were incredibly strong first steps, but as long as 17 veterans die by suicide each day, our work must continue. This Congress, we’ll continue fighting for expanded lethal means counseling to all veterans so Veterans Benefit Administration staff, contractors, community care network providers, and caregivers can provide life saving information to our veterans. We’ll work to make sure community providers have a better understanding of military and veteran culture so they can provide the best treatment possible, and we’ll support efforts for increased outreach to our most at-risk veterans, including women, LGBTQ+, and Native veterans.

317.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities - Addressing the Effects of Toxic Exposure
317.description: We need to recognize toxic exposure as a cost of war. Passing the Blue Water Navy Vietnam Veterans Act last Congress was a massive step to ensure those exposed to toxic substances during their service are cared for, but it took more than 40 years. The burden of proof shouldn’t be on our veterans, and there’s no reason that they and their survivors should have to fight VA for the care and benefits they earned. If America is willing to send our servicemembers into harm’s way to defend our democracy, then she must be willing to ensure we take care of all those who have borne the battle.

318.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities - Creating a Welcoming VA
318.description: VA must recognize the extraordinary diversity of our veteran population — which includes more women, LGBTQ+, Black, Asian, Hispanic, and Native veterans than ever before — and ensure all veterans know they have a place at VA and feel safe and welcomed walking through its doors. VA must also acknowledge the diversity and contributions of its workforce and address systemic discrimination in the workplace. To build a stronger, more welcoming, and more effective VA, we must begin the work to earn back the trust the institution has lost. We need to ensure that VA care and benefits are distributed fairly to all eligible veterans, regardless of social or physical disparities. We are committed to addressing inequities across VA including a focus on underserved veterans from tribal communities, homeless veterans, and deported veterans. No veteran should face barriers to care or benefits they’ve earned — that’s why we must look back to document how veterans were denied benefits, remediate that disparity, and ensure we equitably disburse future benefits to all who have served.

319.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities for Women Veterans
319.description: There are currently more than 2 million servicewomen and women veterans. Thanks to the advocacy of the Women Veterans Task Force, the House passed the Deborah Sampson Act last Congress — the most comprehensive package for women veterans in over a decade, but there’s still more to do. All women deserve to feel safe while accessing high-quality VA care. We must eradicate sexual harassment and assault and other forms of unacceptable behavior at VA facilities. While the Committee is cautiously optimistic regarding changes currently underway at VA to address this issue, we will remain vigilant as the Deborah Sampson Act moves toward implementation.

320.title: Chairman Takano's Priorities for the 117th Congress
320.description:
The Committee was busy during the 116th Congress. From finally getting Blue Water Navy Vietnam veterans the benefits they’ve earned to passing the Veterans’ COMPACT Act and making real strides to reduce veteran suicide, the Committee accomplished a lot on behalf of veterans.

Chairman Takano announced the Committee’s top nine priorities for the 117th Congress. As the country continues to confront the COVID-19 pandemic, the Committee will work to:

• Create a more welcoming VA and build equity for veterans
• Reduce veteran suicide
• Address toxic exposure
• Ensure student veterans receive quality education
• Advocate for women veterans
• Modernize VA
• Support VA’s long term care facilities
• Improve VA’s management and oversight
• Ensure our legislative accomplishments are implemented effectively.

With Secretary McDonough and President Biden — someone who deeply understands the sacrifices service members, veterans, and their families make — we can build back better for our veterans and restore their faith in VA. 

Learn more: https://veterans.house.gov/chairman-takanos-priorities

347.title: Veterans Are Veterans - No Matter What Language They Speak
347.description: Earlier this summer, Committee staff found out that VA did not provide key fact sheets to Spanish speaking veterans in Puerto Rico. Rep Gil Cisneros introduced legislation to fix that & ensure veterans with limited English proficiency can access the benefits they earned.

350.title: Whistleblowers Are Standing Up For Veterans
350.description:
Too many VA whistleblowers face retaliation after reporting. On June 25th, 2019 the House Committee on Veterans Affairs 
held a hearing to address key protections for whistleblowers and the culture of retaliation at VA. Watch to learn about the experiences of some VA whistleblowers.
